newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-BOSRA SHAM WINS CHAMPION STAKES FOR CECIL.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-BOSRA SHAM WINS CHAMPION STAKES FOR CECIL.

text.p: Top filly Bosra Sham, ridden by Pat Eddery, won the Champion Stakes on Saturday, virtually clinching the 1996 trainers' title for Henry Cecil ahead of big rival Saeed bin Suroor.
Bosra Sham (9-4) sprinted clear of even money favourite Halling, trained by bin Suroor and the mount of Frankie Dettori, to lift the $276,000 first prize for owner Wafic Said.
It was a dazzling performance by the 1,000 Guineas winnner Bosra Sham, who has suffered during the season from a foot problem which has restricted her racecourse appearances.
Trainer Cecil, who now looks assured of his 11th title with three weeks of the season left, was near to tears as the filly made her way back to the unsaddling enclosure.
He now enjoys a lead of around 56,000 pounds ($89,000) over bin Suroor, who trains Halling for the Godolphin operation of Sheikh Mohammed.

Cecil used to train for the sheikh but the pair split in acrimonious circumstances just over a year ago leaving observers to wonder whether Cecil could hit the heights again without his leading patron.
But the Newmarket handler has struck back in the most eloquent way and his winnings for the season now stand at around 1.86 million pounds ($2.95 million).
Ironically, Saturday's race, known in full as the Dubai Champion Stakes, was sponsored by Sheik Mohammed and his family.
It was the sheikh who made the presentation to Cecil as winning trainer. The two men shook hands and joked.
Only six contested the race but it was a quality affair with Halling bidding to add the Champion Stakes to earlier group one victories in the York International and Sandown Eclipse Stakes.
Winning jcokey Eddery, describing the horses behind him as among the best in the world, said :" It was just great."
